top_choice_rationale: P001 awards Hidetoshi Katori and Jun Ye for the optical lattice clock: trapping neutral atoms at a magic wavelength removes the trap-induced shift while keeping the signal-to-noise of large ensembles. It is a specific, mature and independently reproduced advance, with clocks compared across laboratories near 1e-18 fractional uncertainty. The two-laureate allocation is defensible, with the citation worded around the invention and development rather than a record figure or the redefinition of the second. The distinctness-from-the-comb objection is a judgement but is answered by the physics. No award is the only alternative on the slate and is clearly worse than a mature, well-defined achievement.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; he is a superconducting-circuit theorist and the candidates are in optical atomic clocks, with no documented link to Katori or Ye.
